title: Legal interpretation and AI: from expert systems to argumentation and LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2603.05392v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: AI and Law research has encountered legal interpretation in different ways, in the context of its evolving approaches and methodologies. Research on expert system has focused on legal knowledge engineering, with the goal of ensuring that human-generated interpretations can be precisely transferred into knowledge-bases, to be consistently applied. Research on argumentation has aimed at representing the structure of interpretive arguments, as well as their dialectical interactions, to assess of the acceptability of interpretive claims within argumentation frameworks. Research on machine learning has focused on the automated generation of interpretive suggestions and arguments, through general and specialised language models, now being increasingly deployed in legal practice.

translated_title: 法律解释与人工智能：从专家系统到论证与大语言模型
translated_abstract: 人工智能与法律研究在其不断演进的方法论背景下，以不同的方式接触到了法律解释问题。专家系统研究聚焦于法律知识工程，其目标是确保人类生成的解释能够被精确地转移到知识库中，从而得到一致的应用。论证研究旨在表征解释性论证的结构及其辩证互动，以在论证框架内评估解释性主张的可接受性。机器学习研究则聚焦于通过通用和专业化语言模型自动生成解释建议和论证，这些模型如今正越来越多地被部署于法律实践之中。
tldr: 本文梳理了人工智能与法律领域处理法律解释问题的三类方法的演进：专家系统的法律知识工程、论证框架对解释性论证结构的表征，以及基于大语言模型的解释建议自动生成。
en_tdlr: This paper surveys how AI and Law research has approached legal interpretation through three evolving paradigms: legal knowledge engineering in expert systems, argumentation frameworks for representing interpretive arguments, and automated generation of interpretations using general and specialized language models increasingly deployed in legal practice.
